title: Lynx Capital — VPC private deployment assessment & phased upgrade playbook (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures the assessment, sizing assumptions, architecture Q&A, Terraform module notes, and a phased upgrade + rollback plan for Lynx Capital's VPC/private deployment of Redwood Inference. Intended audience: Lynx infra team, Redwood private deployments eng, solutions engineering.

Context / constraints:
- Customer: Lynx Capital (investment platform) — strict egress rules, must use customer KMS for model keys, logging stored in S3-compatible bucket inside their VPC.
- Primary workload: low-latency chat inference for trading assistance + nightly batch embeddings for analytics.
- Regulatory: logs must be retained 1 year, audit trail required for model changes.
- Initial target region: us-east-1 (customer-managed VPC). Secondary region: us-west-2 for DR (phase 2).
- Timeline: P0 assessment -> P1 pilot (2-3 months) -> P2 production rollout (quarterly cadence for upgrades).

High-level architecture (assumptions):
- Control plane: Redwood-managed, communicates to customer control-plane proxy via mTLS over private endpoints.
- Data plane: fully in-customer VPC. Serving runtime deployed into customer EKS cluster or bare-metal k8s nodes depending on RFEs.
- KMS: customer will supply AWS KMS key; Redwood will integrate via IAM role assumption.
- Networking: private subnets for GPU nodes, NAT for outbound updates only to Redwood-approved URLs.
- Storage: EBS gp3 for stateful nodes (model cache), S3 (internal) for persistent artifacts.

Sizing & capacity assumptions (initial pilot):
- Workload profile: 60% chat requests (interactive, 0.5–1.5s SLO), 40% batch embeddings (throughput-oriented overnight). 75th pct sequence length ~512 tokens.
- Models: ensemble of a 7B generation model (quantized) and an embedding model (2B). Primary serve: quantized int8 7B on A10G-like instances for pilot.
- Target concurrency: sustained 60 qps of single-user chat with p50 latency < 400ms per token generation and p95 < 900ms (pilot SLOs relaxed).
- Pilot node types & counts (T-shirt estimate):
  - 3 x GPU nodes (A10G equivalent) with 48 GB GPU RAM for generation shards (support continuous batching + KV).
  - 2 x GPU nodes (A10G equivalent) for embedding workers (optimized for throughput).
  - 2 x control-plane (m small) for sidecar services (autoscaler, metrics scraper).
  - 3 x infra nodes (control-plane helpers, model registry cache) – use c5d-style.
- Storage: 1 TB EBS per GPU node for model cache/temp, 2 TB shared S3.
- Networking: 25 Gbps NICs on GPU nodes recommended to avoid tail latency on KV fetches.

Terraform module notes / changes required:
- Modules to consume: redwood/priv-deploy/vpc (network), redwood/priv-deploy/eks (k8s), redwood/priv-deploy/gpu-pool (instance definitions), redwood/priv-deploy/kms (kms-binding).
- Required provider versions: terraform >=1.5.0, aws provider >=4.50.0.
- New vars to add for Lynx:
  - customer_kms_key_arn (string)
  - allowed_egress_endpoints (list of string)
  - enable_private_link_control_plane (bool)
  - gpu_node_instance_types (list)
- Recommended practice: keep module outputs minimal and emit resource IDs needed for Redwood agent bootstrap only. Avoid exposing secrets in terraform state; use lifecycle "prevent_destroy" on kms alias binding resources.
- Workaround: Lynx's strict subnet tagging requires optional mapping in vpc module: additional_subnet_tags map(string). We'll create a patch in terraform modules to inject tags.
- Upgrade notes: Add a feature-flag in module to toggle live-kv-cache migration (safe default off).

Operational runbook (pilot -> prod):
Phase 0 — assessment (this doc)
  - Complete network flow diagram with Lynx networking team. Confirm NAT/egress constraints and approved outbound endpoints.
  - Validate KMS ARNs and IAM role trust.
  - Confirm storage throughput SLAs (EBS & S3).

Phase 1 — pilot deployment (2 weeks):
  - Deploy infra in non-prod VPC, enable rolling logs -> internal S3 path.
  - Install Redwood agent with minimal permission set; register initial model artifacts.
  - Run focused load test (50 qps spike test, long-tail sequences) and capture token-level latencies.
  - Observe KV cache hit ratio; tune batch window to balance latency/cost.
  - Run security review and penetration checklist.

Phase 2 — staggered prod rollout (4–8 weeks):
  - Canary route 10% traffic -> pilot cluster for 48–72 hours. Verify quality metrics (per-prompt eval set) and latency.
  - Increase to 50% then 100% after success criteria met.
  - Schedule weekly checks for first month: cost per token, p95 latency, error rate, KMS encrypt/decrypt ops.

Upgrade & migration strategy (major runtime upgrades):
- Principle: prefer blue-green with warm cache transfer where possible. For major runtime changes that invalidate KV cache format, perform cross-compatibility tests in a staging environment.
- Steps:
  1) Create parallel cluster with upgraded runtime in same VPC (smaller capacity).
  2) Warm models onto new cluster using synthetic traffic (model pinning).
  3) Run A/B tests with 5–10% traffic. Monitor for degradations (embedding drift, hallucination rate).
  4) If metrics stable for 72h, increase traffic to 50% then shift.
  5) Decommission old cluster after 7 days of stable operations.
- Rollback: keep old cluster running and traffic-shift back if quality regressions exceed thresholds. Have a pre-approved IAM role for quick model rollback (ensure model registry version pin).

Testing & verification matrix (pilot):
- Smoke tests: agent heartbeat, KMS encryption/decryption, model artifact checksum, container start.
- Perf tests: 95th token latency, time-to-first-token, end-to-end p99.
- Quality tests: run 500 prompts from Lynx eval set against both clusters and compare similarity metrics + hallucination flags.
- Integration: certificate rotation test (mTLS), load balancer failover, node replacement simulation.

Open questions (to resolve with Lynx infra/security):
- Can the customer grant an IAM role for KMS decrypt only to a Redwood-assumed role, or do we need a cross-account KMS key policy?
- Are there egress-proxy appliances that will rewrite TLS SNI? (impacts control plane connectivity)
- Does Lynx require air-gapped software delivery (tarball via internal S3) or is outbound package fetch acceptable from restricted endpoints?
- Disaster recovery RTO/RPO targets for the inference workload? (affects replication strategy and region choices)

Security & compliance reminders:
- Audit logs: ensure model-download events, serve events (summary), and KMS decrypt events are routed to Lynx's audit log stream + Redwood control-plane audit.
- Secrets: use IRSA (IAM Roles for Service Accounts) where possible; do not store private keys in plaintext in EBS snapshots.
- Pen test: schedule joint pen-test window before production rollout; share a lightweight attack plan.

Checklist (quick):
[ ] Network diagram sign-off
[ ] KMS policy validated
[ ] Terraform module vars finalized
[ ] Pilot infra deployed and smoke-tested
[ ] Load test results collected and reviewed
[ ] Canary rollout plan scheduled
[ ] Runbook for rollback published

Notes / raw observations from the assessment call (controller notes, shorthand):
- Lynx uses internal egress proxy for vulnerability scanning. Need to get exact proxy list; might force us to pre-bundle container images.
- Customer asked for explicit cost cap alarms at 10% over forecast during first 30 days. Add billing exporter + alert.
- They prefer A10G-equivalent GPUs but asked for a plan to switch to T4s for lower cost in non-latency-critical paths — include autoscaling group with mixed instance policy.
- Suggest we include a small read-only replica in us-west-2 (spot-backed) for nightly batch embeddings failover.

Next steps / owners:
- Maya: update terraform module patch for subnet tag mapping (ETA 2025-01-20)
- Arjun: draft KMS trust policy and share with Lynx (ETA 2025-01-15)
- Sofia: prepare pilot load-test harness + eval set (ETA 2025-01-22)
- Diego: coordinate security checklist / pen-test window with Lynx sec contact (ETA 2025-02-01)

Appendix (quick numbers snapshot):
- Estimated pilot monthly infra cost (EC2/EBS/network): ~$12k–18k (A10G-like on-demand assumption).
- Estimated model storage: 500GB active + 1TB archive.
- Expected batch embedding window: 3–5 hours overnight at 200–400 qps.

If anything in this doc conflicts with contract language, default to the contract. This remains a working draft — will iterate after the next alignment call on 2025-01-16.
